script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

EXT. NEW YORK CITY - DAY

A bustling metropolis. People rushing past each other on the sidewalks, horns honking in the streets. Our HERO, JAMES, a 40-something, slightly disheveled MAN, walks slowly amongst the crowd, looking lost and dejected.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

James sits at a table in a cozy, quirky coffee shop. He slumps in his chair, staring at his laptop. He's a struggling writer, and this latest project has been his undoing.

BARISTA (offscreen)
Can I get you another cup?

James looks up, starts.

JAMES
(sighs)
No, thank you. I think I've had enough for today.

The barista exits. James leans back in his chair, rubs his eyes, and stares blankly at his laptop.

INT. JAMES' APARTMENT - NIGHT

James sits on the couch, surrounded by takeout containers, empty beer bottles, and papers covered in scribbled notes. His cat, FLUFFY, meows plaintively.

Suddenly, there's a knock on the door. James groans and stands up to answer it.

IT'S MARY, an old friend he hasn't seen in years. She's put on a few pounds, her hair has gone gray, but she still has that warm, welcoming smile.

MARY
(laughs)
James, it's good to see you. I've come to take you out for dinner.

James is surprised but grateful. They go out to eat and catch up on old times. Mary tells James about her successful career as a baker, her loving husband, and her two wonderful children. James feels a pang of jealousy but hides it well.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

James sits in the same seat at the coffee shop, now with a fresh cup of coffee and a notebook. He looks at it, then at Mary, who is sitting across the room, working on her laptop.

He starts to write. The words flow easily, inspired by Mary's success and their rekindled friendship.

EXT. CENTRAL PARK - DAY

James and Mary walk through Central Park, laughing and enjoying each other's company. They come across a street performer, playing a beautiful melody on the violin.

Mary stops and turns to James.

MARY
Do you remember that time we came here and you wrote a whole poem about the sunset?

James smiles.

JAMES
Yes, I do. That was the first time I ever thought I might have a future as a writer.

Mary looks thoughtful.

MARY
You know, I think it's not too late for you.

INT. JAMES' APARTMENT - NIGHT

James sits at his desk, surrounded by piles of manuscripts, notes, and research. He's writing every day, and the words are flowing freely. He's starting to believe in himself again.

Fluffy curls up at his feet, purring contentedly.

INT. LITERARY AGENT'S OFFICE - DAY

James sits nervously in the waiting room of a prestigious literary agent's office. He's wearing a nice suit and carrying a folder full of his work.

The agent calls him in. They discuss James' writing, and the agent is impressed. She offers him a contract, and James is elated.

EXT. NEW YORK CITY - NIGHT

James walks through the city, feeling alive and invigorated. He's got a second chance at his dream, and he's not going to waste it.

He stops at a street corner and looks up at the night sky. He takes out a pen and a piece of paper and starts to write.

FADE OUT.

THE END
